# Bundles

How nself records which bundles are installed and why each plugin is present.

## The bundle ledger

Each project keeps one machine-owned file, `.nself/state/bundles.json`. It is the install-state ledger, contract `cli.bundle-ledger` v1. Its JSON Schema is `schemas/bundle-ledger.v1.schema.json`.

The file starts with `"_generated": "GENERATED BY nself — DO NOT HAND EDIT"`. nself writes it; do not edit it. A hand-edited or damaged ledger is reported as an error with the file path, never silently replaced.

```json
{
  "_generated": "GENERATED BY nself — DO NOT HAND EDIT",
  "schema_version": 1,
  "bundles": {
    "chat": { "installed_at": "2026-10-10T12:00:00Z" }
  },
  "plugins": {
    "bots": {
      "installed_by": ["chat"],
      "explicit": false,
      "tier": "licensed",
      "version": "1.2.0",
      "checksum": ""
    }
  }
}
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `bundles.<slug>.installed_at` | When the bundle was recorded as installed (RFC 3339, UTC). |
| `plugins.<slug>.installed_by` | The installed bundles that reference the plugin, sorted. |
| `plugins.<slug>.explicit` | True when the plugin was installed on its own, so removing a bundle must keep it. |
| `plugins.<slug>.tier` | `free` or `licensed`. |
| `plugins.<slug>.version` | The installed version. |
| `plugins.<slug>.checksum` | Lowercase hex sha256 of the installed artifact, empty when none was recorded. |

A plugin record exists only while `installed_by` is not empty or `explicit` is true.

## How it is written

- Writers take an OS lock on `bundles.json.lock` (next to the ledger), write a temp file in the same directory, fsync it, and rename it over the ledger. A reader sees the old file or the new one, never a partial file.
- A crash between the temp write and the rename leaves the previous ledger intact.
- The file is mode 0644 (it holds no secret) in a 0700 directory.
- Windows is supported through WSL2, where the lock applies.

## Remove rule

A bundle remove may delete a plugin only when the bundle was the last one in its `installed_by` and `explicit` is false. A plugin that another installed bundle still references, or that was installed on its own, stays. The ledger package implements the rule (`RemoveBundle`); wiring it into `nself bundle remove` is a separate change.

## First use (bootstrap)

When no ledger exists, nself derives one from the installed plugin directories and the bundle membership in `bundles.json`:

- A bundle counts as installed when it can be installed as a unit and every member plugin is installed.
- `installed_by` lists every installed bundle that contains the plugin (bundles may overlap).
- A plugin in no installed bundle is `explicit: true`.

Bootstrap cannot tell a plugin you installed yourself from one a bundle installed, if a bundle later covers it. It treats that plugin as bundle-owned. Installs recorded after the ledger exists are exact.

A plugin or bundle whose name is not a valid slug cannot be recorded; bootstrap skips it and prints a warning. If the installed plugins cannot be read, there is no bootstrap: nself reports the error and writes nothing, rather than recording an empty ledger.

`nself bundle list --json` reads the ledger; the plain table never loads it. When the file does not exist it computes the bootstrap view in memory and writes nothing.

## `nself bundle list --json`

Each row of the JSON array gains an additive `ledger` object, that bundle's slice of the ledger:

```json
{
  "slug": "chat",
  "ledger": {
    "installed": true,
    "installed_at": "2026-10-10T12:00:00Z",
    "plugins": [
      { "slug": "bots", "installed_by": ["chat"], "explicit": false, "tier": "licensed", "version": "1.2.0", "checksum": "" }
    ]
  }
}
```

`installed` is false and `installed_at` is absent for a bundle that is not recorded as installed. `plugins` lists the bundle's member plugins that the ledger records, and is `[]` when there are none. All earlier fields are unchanged.

See also [[cmd-bundle]].
